subject: Clarify: which Redwood deployments should we include in FinApps' penetration test?
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@finapps.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finapps.io
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test evidence — which Redwood deployments count for our SIG + CAIQ

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — FinApps' procurement team is working through the SIG/CAIQ and our security team needs to know exactly which Redwood-managed deployments we can rely on for your penetration test report. Specifically: 

- Are the Hosted API endpoints (api.redwood.ai) included?
- Do Dedicated pools you run for customers fall under the same coverage?
- For Private/VPC deployments where Redwood manages the control plane but customer supplies VPC, what components are covered?
- For the on-prem installer customers run entirely in their datacenter, do you provide any pen test evidence or guidance?

We're trying to finalize the reliance statement in the SIG and also decide whether to run an independent test (vendor-led) vs relying on Redwood's report. Can you also share a redacted copy of the most recent pen test report and a short remediation summary with dates?

Our timeline is tight — procurement wants confirmation by Monday.

Appreciate the help,
Alice
Alice Chen
Director, Security & Compliance, FinApps
---
Attachment: none

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finapps.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, security@finapps.io
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence — which Redwood deployments count for our SIG + CAIQ

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then I’ll attach the report and a scope matrix.

1) Hosted (api.redwood.ai) — INCLUDED. Our external-facing hosted API endpoints and the shared control plane are covered by Redwood’s annual penetration test and external third-party assessment. Redacted report attached.

2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools managed by Redwood) — INCLUDED. Dedicated capacity that Redwood manages (compute + network in our cloud accounts dedicated to the customer) is covered by our test when the infrastructure is under Redwood operational control.

3) Private / VPC deployments (Redwood-managed control plane, customer VPC) — PARTIAL. Control plane components that we operate (authentication, orchestration, model registry) are in-scope. Customer-managed VPC networking, security groups, and customer-side compute are out-of-scope for our test — but we provide a deployment checklist and recommended hardening steps. If you want Redwood to include the customer VPC in our test, we can negotiate an add-on scope (requires access window, billable effort, and coordination).

4) On-prem (customer installs full stack on-prem) — OUT OF SCOPE. The on-prem package is maintained as a deliverable but we do not perform the customer’s internal penetration tests. We provide a CIS-style hardening guide and the security package (SBOM, config checklist), and can support a third-party assessor with a point-of-contact and artifact access.

I’ll attach the most recent redacted pen test report and a one-page matrix that maps "covered vs not covered" per deployment type, plus a remediation tracker excerpt showing open items and planned retest dates.

If you need a one-line sentence to put in the SIG reliance statement, feel free to use: 

"FinApps may rely on Redwood Inference’s penetration test report for Redwood-managed hosted and dedicated deployments; customer-managed VPC and on-prem deployments are not covered unless explicitly included via add-on scope."

Happy to jump on a quick call if procurement wants to walk through specifics.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood_pt_report_2028_redacted.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finapps.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, security@finapps.io
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence — which Redwood deployments count for our SIG + CAIQ

Hi Alice — looping in a short checklist for procurement to make the path forward simple: 

- If you rely on Hosted + Dedicated coverage: mark the SIG reliance box and we will provide the redacted report (attached) + the remediation snapshot.
- If you need Private/VPC included: let us know the VPC project name and we’ll send a scope add-on estimate (typically 2–4 engineer-days + 3rd-party assessor fees).
- If you plan to run your own on-prem test: we’ll provide the installer hardening guide and a named Redwood contact for artifact support.

I’ve attached a short remediation tracker excerpt for items relevant to Dedicated deployments and the proposed language for the SIG reliance. If you confirm which option FinApps wants by EOD Monday we’ll produce a signed artifact for procurement.

Next steps: please confirm which environments you intend to rely on and if you want an add-on scope for your VPC.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: remediation_tracker_finapps.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finapps.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, dl@thirdpartysec.com
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pen test evidence — which Redwood deployments count for our SIG + CAIQ

Thanks all — quick operational clarifications to close the loop for procurement and security: 

- The attached scope matrix (redwood_pt_scope_matrix.csv) explicitly lists components we test: control plane APIs, orchestration layer, model-serving runtime in Redwood-managed accounts, and gateway endpoints.
- Excluded by default: customer VPC subnets, customer-managed NAT/GW, on-prem networks, and third-party tenant-managed connectors.
- Open remediation status: 6 medium issues and 2 low issues affecting Dedicated pools; mitigation work is scheduled across April and a retest window is booked for 2028-05-10 to verify closures.
- Evidence provided: redwood_pt_report_2028_redacted.pdf (redacted for customer identifiers), remediation_tracker_finapps.xlsx excerpt. Full technical evidence can be shared under NDA and an artifacts access request if FinApps security needs raw logs or scan outputs.

If FinApps confirms they will rely on Redwood's report for Hosted + Dedicated, we will provide a signed cover letter for procurement and a brief reliance statement they can add to the SIG/CAIQ. If they need us to include the Private VPC, we’ll provide an SOW and schedule.

Ping me if you want a 20-minute call tomorrow to run procurement through the reliance language.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
